## Trellis: Episode Publish (YouTube)

Last phase of the Episode pipeline. Downloads the rendered `video.mp4`, uploads it to YouTube, then writes the URL back to Trellis and marks the publication **live**.

**Webhook:** `https://n8n.sproutify.app/webhook/trellis-episode-publish` (= `EPISODE_PUBLISH_WEBHOOK`)
**Fired by:** `episodeService.publishEpisode` with `{ publication_id, episode_id, branch, platform:'youtube', video_url, metadata:{title,description,tags,chapters,hashtags} }`.

### FLOW
Webhook → **Build Metadata** (Code: title / description+chapters+hashtags / tags, trimmed to YT limits) → **Mark Uploading** → **Download Video** (GET video_url → binary `data`) → **YouTube Upload** (category 10 = Music) → **Mark Live** (publication → live + external_url) → **Update Episode** (youtube_url + status published).

### SETUP
1. **YouTube Upload node** → set **Credential → your Google/YouTube OAuth2 account** (the one you connected). Category is 10 (Music) — change if needed.
2. **The 3 Supabase nodes** (Mark Uploading / Mark Live / Update Episode) → set **Credential → your existing Trellis (Hub) Supabase account**. No key to paste — these tables (`trellis_episode_publications`, `trellis_episodes`) live on the Hub, the same project your music-session nodes already write to.
3. **Verify node fields after import** — the YouTube node's field names can vary by n8n version (title / categoryId / binaryProperty / options.privacyStatus / options.description / options.tags). Re-map any that didn't import.

### NOTES
- **Unverified app caveat:** while your Google OAuth app is in Testing / unverified, uploads using the `youtube.upload` scope are forced **private and locked** by YouTube regardless of `privacyStatus`, until the app is verified. For your own channel you can flip them public in YouTube Studio, or submit the app for verification.
- The whole video is buffered in memory for the upload — fine for short/medium tracks; very long (multi-hour) renders may need a resumable-upload approach.
- No failure branch here for brevity — add an error path that sets the publication to `status:'failed'` if you want the UI to reflect upload errors.
